clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man with known MDS-MLD (diagnosed 6 years prior) presented to dermatology with a 2-year history of acute photosensitivity characterized by burning pain and excruciating skin discomfort after 30 minutes of sun exposure on the face, hands, and fingertips, followed by crusting skin lesions on the dorsa of the hands. Physical examination revealed chronic photodamage with thickened lichenified skin, fresh blister, crusts, indented scars, and milia on sun-exposed areas (dorsa of hands, neck, face). Diagnostic workup demonstrated massively elevated plasma free protoporphyrin (30 umol/L, normal <0.20) and total porphyrins (33.9 umol/L, normal <1.30) with positive plasma fluorescence scan. Skin biopsy confirmed subepidermal blistering with scarce inflammatory reaction consistent with porphyria. CBC confirmed ongoing cytopenias consistent with underlying MDS. The diagnosis of acquired EPP secondary to MDS was established based on the clinical phenotype, massively elevated protoporphyrin levels, histopathological findings, and the temporal relationship to underlying myelodysplasia (symptom onset 4 years after MDS diagnosis in adulthood). Two-year follow-up demonstrated successful control with sun-protective measures without need for afamelanotide, and no development of liver toxicity despite persistently elevated plasma porphyrin levels with regular monitoring.

Skin biopsy confirmed subepidermal blistering with scarce inflammatory reaction consistent with porphyria. CBC confirmed ongoing cytopenias consistent with underlying MDS. The diagnosis of acquired EPP secondary to MDS was established based on the clinical phenotype, massively elevated protoporphyrin levels, histopathological findings, and the temporal relationship to underlying myelodysplasia (symptom onset 4 years after MDS diagnosis in adulthood). Two-year follow-up demonstrated successful control with sun-protective measures without need for afamelanotide, and no development of liver toxicity despite persistently elevated plasma porphyrin levels with regular monitoring.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient has underlying myelodysplastic syndrome with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) diagnosed 6 years prior to presentation
Two-year history of acute photosensitivity with burning pain and excruciating skin discomfort on face, hands, and fingertips after 30 minutes of sun exposure
Crusting skin lesions appearing days after sun exposure on dorsa of hands
Physical examination shows chronic photodamage: thickened lichenified skin, fresh blister, numerous crusts, indented scars, and milia formation on dorsa of hands, neck, and face
Massively elevated plasma free protoporphyrin (30 umol/L, normal <0.20) and total porphyrins (33.9 umol/L, normal <1.30) with positive plasma fluorescence scan
Skin biopsy demonstrates subepidermal blistering with scarce inflammatory reaction consistent with porphyria
CBC demonstrates anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukopenia consistent with underlying MDS
Two-year post-diagnosis outcome: controlled with sun-protective measures, no afamelanotide required, no liver toxicity despite high plasma porphyrins, undergoing regular monitoring

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Late onset of symptoms at age 71 (4 years after MDS diagnosis) without reported childhood photosensitivity or family history, consistent with acquired form secondary to clonal hematopoiesis

Clinical presentation of acute burning pain with sun exposure and massively elevated plasma protoporphyrin rather than uroporphyrin; histopathology showing subepidermal blistering without typical PCT features
No documented elevation of urinary porphyrins or mixed porphyrin pattern; clinical picture dominated by acute photosensitivity with protoporphyrin elevation
